issuer: the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), the National Driver's Licence, with testing by the state's Vehicle Inspection Office and payment registered at the state Board of Internal Revenue

licence.name: National Driver's Licence, class B (motor vehicle, private)

note: Read 2026-10-30. The FRSC's licence portal (nigeriadriverslicence.frsc.gov.ng), its FAQ 'How much will the New Licence Cost me?': class A (motorcycle) N7,000 for 3 years or N11,000 for 5 years; other classes N15,000 for 3 years or N21,000 for 5 years, each class charged separately, with possible payment-channel charges. Until 2026-10-30 the 5-year licence for a class other than A was held alone (N21,000, 5 years); from then both terms are held, 3 years at N15,000 and 5 at N21,000. The FRSC's Service Charter (undated; it cites the FRSC's annual reports to 2013), Appendix C, 'Requirements and procedure for driver's licence (private class only)': step 1, the applicant is 18 years and above; the test is by the Vehicle Inspection Office and the payment registered at the Board of Internal Revenue. The driving school, the medical certificate and the state's test fees aren't held. No identity card is held, and no exchange list was read.
